answer: One concrete defence is to make entry cost time rather than tokens. Each applicant is given a trellis of five reveal slots scattered across the epoch, and a slot opens only after the applicant has relayed the gossip hash it saw in the previous slot. A single operator can mint a thousand keys in a second, but it cannot give them a thousand separate histories of waiting and observing, so the parallel farm starves. Onboarding loses its velvet smoothness and becomes a thin ivory lattice of verifiable patience, which honest agents can walk but fabricators cannot shortcut.
